history.summary: Built by Rani Rashmoni, a zamindar and Kali devotee, after a dream vision in which Kali asked for a temple on the Hooghly instead of a pilgrimage to Kashi. Constructed 1847-1855 by the firm Mackintosh Burn on land bought from James Hasty (the 'Saheban Bagicha'). Navaratna (nine-spired) Bengal architecture inspired by the Radhakanta temple of Tollygunge; three-storeyed, ~100 ft high. The complex holds twelve aat-chala Shiva shrines, a Radha-Krishna temple, a bathing ghat and a shrine to Rani Rashmoni. First priest Ramkumar Chhattopadhyay was succeeded by his younger brother Gadadhar - the mystic Ramakrishna - with wife Sarada Devi in the Nahabat; their presence made it a world-famous shrine. Local tradition also counts it among Shakti Peethas (Sati's tongue said to have fallen here - verify). TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists town as 'Kolkata'; corrected to Dakshineswar, North 24 Parganas (Kamarhati municipality; part of Greater Kolkata).

name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
town_description: Dakshineswar is a historic locality in Kamarhati municipality, North 24 Parganas, on the eastern bank of the Hooghly river, within Greater Kolkata. It is famed for the Kali temple and as the 19th-century home of the mystic Ramakrishna.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~18-20 km)
travel.railway: Dakshineswar railway station (suburban line); Sealdah ~12 km
travel.road: Rani Rashmoni Road / B.T. Road; Dakshineswar metro station (Blue Line); buses and taxis. Ferry across the Hooghly to Belur Math.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, early morning (7:00-8:30 AM) to avoid queues; Tuesday and Saturday considered auspicious.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM-12:30 PM; evening 3:00/3:30 PM-8:30/9:00 PM depending on season, with a mid-day break. Entry free. Sources conflict on exact evening timings (verify). Festivals like Kali Puja alter hours.
